message.content: {"pharmakon_274e":{"rendering":"medicine","gloss":"medicine","category":"remedy/medicine","note":"Appears in the clause 'it being a medicine which I have discovered , both for memory and wisdom'; the stray space before the comma is in the OCR text."},"mneme_274e":{"rendering":"memory","gloss":"memory","note":"Also 'better able to remember' earlier, but the genitive of the pharmakon clause is 'for memory'."},"sophia_274e":{"rendering":"wisdom","gloss":"wisdom","note":""},"pharmakon_275a":{"rendering":"medicine","gloss":"medicine","category":"remedy/medicine","note":"Same word as at 274e, so Thamus reuses Theuth's term. Wright writes 'Your discovery, therefore, is a medicine not for memory, but for recollection'."},"mneme_275a":{"rendering":"memory","gloss":"memory","note":"Same word as at 274e."},"hypomnesis_275a":{"rendering":"recollection","gloss":"recollection","note":"Glossed immediately as 'for recalling to, not for keeping in mind', which explains the contrast. 'Recollection' is also used earlier for the verb anamimneskomenous ('they will recollect'), so the hypomnesis/anamnesis distinction is blurred."},"sophia_275a":{"rendering":"a show of wisdom without the reality","gloss":"an appearance of wisdom lacking the reality","note":"Doxa is rendered 'a show' and aletheia 'the reality' in a looser form; the opposition 'not truth' becomes 'without the reality'."},"doxosophoi_275b":{"rendering":"wise in their own conceit","gloss":"wise in their own conceit","note":"Wright expands the compound into a phrase; the contrast with sophoi is given as 'instead of truly wise'. The sense is 'conceited' rather than 'seeming wise', which shifts the emphasis from appearance to self-opinion."},"argument":"Wright uses 'medicine' for both occurrences of pharmakon, so Thamus turns Theuth's own word against him: it is a medicine, but for recollection, not memory. This keeps the argument legible and tidy, yet it settles the word as a healing term and removes any hint of poison or ambivalence. 'Memory'/'recollection' also keeps the mneme/hypomnesis contrast, though 'recollection' blurs it with anamnesis, and 'wise in their own conceit' makes the final charge about vanity rather than mere seeming."}
